generalfeedback.text: Command turns a request into a standalone object exposing execute(), which is what enables undo, queuing, and logging.

questiontext.text: Which two roles does Command decouple from each other?

feedback.text: Correct — the invoker triggers execute() without knowing the receiver.
That separation belongs to MVC.
That belongs to Publish-Subscribe.
That belongs to Pipes and Filters.

generalfeedback.text: The invoker holds a Command and calls execute(); the concrete command forwards work to the receiver, so the two never reference each other directly.

questiontext.text: Because a command records the request, which feature is naturally supported?

feedback.text: Correct — storing commands lets you reverse or replay them.
That is unrelated to the pattern.
That is a runtime feature, not from Command.
Not what the pattern provides.

generalfeedback.text: Keeping command objects in a history enables undo/redo; keeping them in a list enables queuing and logging.

questiontext.text: A command that groups several commands and executes them as one unit is called a ______.

feedback.text: Correct — it composes multiple commands.
Singleton is about a single instance, not grouping.
A null command does nothing; it does not group commands.
A proxy stands in for another object; it is not a group.

generalfeedback.text: A macro (composite) command holds a list of commands and calls execute() on each, enabling batch operations.
